descriptions.value: An incorrect authorization flaw was found in AWX, the automation controller component of Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform. The API access classes for JobTemplate and WorkflowJobTemplate do not check the caller's Credential use_role when assigning the single-valued webhook_credential foreign key: JobTemplateAccess.can_add/can_change and WorkflowJobTemplateAccess.can_change in awx/main/access.py omit the check_related('webhook_credential', Credential, ..., role_field='use_role') call that UnifiedCredentialsMixin.can_attach performs for the normal many-to-many credentials relationship, and the serializer validates only the credential's type and namespace. A user who may administer their own job template (or workflow job template) and use its project and inventory can therefore attach a webhook token credential (for example a GitLab token) that they do not have use permission on. The template administrator can retrieve the template's webhook key; a subsequent webhook event causes AWX to decrypt the attached token and send it in the request header (for GitLab, PRIVATE-TOKEN) to a status URL derived from the event payload, disclosing the victim's token to a destination the attacker can influence. This may disclose another user's personal access token and allow whatever actions that token permits.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to retrieve server secrets through the /api/v1/config/defaults endpoint. Attackers can send a GET request to obtain the operator's LLM provider API keys and GitHub or GitLab tokens, then abuse those services and accessible repositories.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.5 through 3.8.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows registered users to leak server-wide GitLab or Gitea tokens via repository_url. Attackers can create a gitlab or gitea project pointing to a controlled host and request its branches to capture the operator's token and reach internal hosts.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.10 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read CI/CD variable metadata from projects they did not have access to due to improper authorization in pipeline execution policies.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 14.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to create issues with locked discussions despite lacking the required permissions due to improper authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 13.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to view iteration details from private groups they did not have access to due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.7 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read GitLab Duo seat assignments and usage data from other groups due to improper authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read files from a project's private repository due to missing authorization checks in snippets.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of users viewing a wiki page due to improper sanitization of user input.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.12 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read private CI/CD template files from projects they did not have access to due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 16.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the browser of users viewing Error Tracking pages due to improper sanitization of user input.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 8.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to import Git repositories into projects despite administrator restrictions on import sources due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 8.12 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read Git LFS objects from restricted projects due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read Git LFS objects from projects restricted by External Authorization due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.1.7 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed sensitive credential values submitted in GraphQL requests to be written to logs in plaintext due to incomplete filtering of sensitive data.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.0 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to hide changes from reviewers in merge request diffs due to improper handling of file names.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an individual controlling an upstream repository to alter cached Maven packages from other repositories in the same virtual registry due to improper response validation.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read NuGet package metadata that should not have been accessible due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to enable Amazon Q automatic code reviews on a project despite an administrator lock due to improper enforcement of instance-level settings.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with a valid agent token to cause a denial of service in the GitLab agent server (KAS) due to improper input validation.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to view unredacted secret values from secret detection findings they had access to through GitLab Duo Agent Platform due to improper authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.11 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read commit comments from a private source fork through a public project's merge request discussions due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read private CI/CD job artifacts belonging to other projects through GitLab Pages due to improper validation of file paths.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read restricted job artifact data due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to change the GitLab Duo Code Review consent setting of a parent group due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 16.10 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to configure GitLab Duo settings for groups without an eligible license due to missing authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 18.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to access GitLab Duo features restricted by group-based access rules due to improper handling of failed updates to those rules.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 18.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding an MCP-scoped OAuth token to perform unauthorized issuable state changes on issues and merge requests, including approving and merging, due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 17.4 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to cause a denial of service affecting Duo usage analytics due to improper input validation.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 11.11 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to make requests to internal network services through repository import functionality due to insufficient validation of destination addresses.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to start a Duo Workflow session with elevated privileges beyond those declared by the foundational flow due to improper enforcement of privilege boundaries in certain client environments.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with an unconfirmed email address to be automatically granted Group Owner-level membership during a group import operation, due to insufficient email verification enforcement in the member identity mapping process.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with developer-role permissions to bypass admin-configured AI tool governance controls in a governed namespace due to improper binding of authorization tokens to their intended workflow execution context.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.8 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with planner-role permissions to set a future merge scheduling date on merge requests they authored, a capability restricted to developer-role permissions and above, due to insufficient permission enforcement on the merge scheduling field during merge request updates.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 12.10 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an unauthenticated user to read private project metadata from packages published by other projects due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 13.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user with owner-role permissions to execute arbitrary JavaScript in another user's browser through the Confluence integration due to improper input validation.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 9.3 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to access protected CI/CD variables and resources due to a race condition in pipeline job authorization.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 19.2 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user holding a granular personal access token with limited scope to authorize Kubernetes API proxy access beyond the token's intended boundaries due to missing granular scope enforcement in the Kubernetes agent proxy-user authorization flow.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab EE affecting all versions from 19.1 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to run code in protected pipelines through a scheduled pipeline execution policy after the policy had been unassigned due to incorrect authorization checks.

GitLab has remediated an issue in GitLab CE/EE affecting all versions from 17.6 before 19.3.9, 19.4 before 19.4.8, and 19.5 before 19.5.6 that under certain conditions could have allowed an authenticated user to read Kubernetes Secrets from other namespaces in clusters connected through the GitLab agent for Kubernetes due to incorrect authorization in workspaces.

matrix-hookshot is a Matrix bot for connecting to external services like GitHub, GitLab, JIRA, and more. Prior to 7.3.3, Hookshot can crash in src/Bridge.ts while processing a modern Matrix reply whose m.relates_to.m.in_reply_to.event_id identifies an event that the bot cannot read. Bridge event handling calls botClient.getEvent() for the parent event without catching the resulting M_NOT_FOUND error, allowing the rejected request to escape reply processing and terminate the service. This issue is fixed in version 7.3.3.

Mattermost versions 11.7.x <= 11.7.11, 11.10.x <= 11.10.2, 11.11.x <= 11.11.1 fail to enforce the configured GitLab group/namespace restriction on the permalink code-preview feature and the {{get_projects}} MCP tool, which allows an authenticated user with a connected GitLab account to retrieve repository file content or project metadata from projects outside the restricted group via a crafted GitLab permalink or MCP tool call. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00750

Mattermost Plugins versions <=12.-1 11.11.7 11.2.10 11.1.11.0 fail to enforce the GitLab project permission check for confidential issues when the project is publicly visible which allows an authenticated user with no GitLab membership in the project to obtain the contents of confidential issues, including title, description, author, and URL via subscribing a channel to the parent public GitLab group with the confidential_issues feature and waiting for a confidential issue webhook event. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00738
In JetBrains YouTrack before 2026.2.19840 improper authorization allowed project administrators to obtain GitLab tokens of other projects

Portainer Community Edition and Business Edition 2.39.0 before 2.45.1 contain a server-side request forgery vulnerability because user-supplied URLs are only syntax-checked by validate.IsURL without resolved address validation. Authenticated users can abuse Git cloning, Helm retrieval, registry ping, or the GitLab proxy to reach loopback, internal, and cloud metadata addresses, probing ports and reading responses.

Lightdash before 3.212.0 contains an insufficiently protected credentials vulnerability in getGitlabInstallationRepoReadAccess that sends the organization GitLab app token to unverified hosts. Project developers can set the dbt connection host_domain to an attacker-controlled server and capture the token when the AI agent reads the repository, gaining access to every reachable repository.
